Lahmacun

Paper-thin Turkish flatbread spread with spiced minced lamb and baked in a fierce oven for four minutes. Rolled up with parsley, onion and a hard squeeze of lemon.

★★★★★★★★★★4.7(1,188)Rated 4.7 out of 5 from 1188 reviews 50 min total Serves 6 servings Medium Turkish
Jump to Recipe Jump to Method

Why This Recipe Works

The topping is spread almost translucently thin so it cooks through in the same four minutes the base takes — a thick layer would leave raw meat over a burnt crust. Grating the vegetables and squeezing them dry stops the topping releasing water and steaming the dough soft.

Method

Tap a step to highlight it, or turn on Cook Mode for large type and step-by-step focus.

  1. Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the warm water and olive oil, and knead 8 minutes until smooth. Prove, covered, for 1 hour until doubled.

  2. Grate the onion, pepper and tomatoes, then squeeze each one hard in a cloth. The topping must be almost dry.

  3. Combine the lamb with the squeezed vegetables, garlic, tomato purée, pepper paste, parsley, spices and salt. Mix thoroughly with your hands into a spreadable paste and refrigerate 30 minutes.

  4. Heat the oven to its maximum, at least 250°C / 480°F, with a baking steel or heavy tray inside for 45 minutes.

  5. Divide the dough into six. Roll each as thin as you can, 25 cm across and almost translucent, using flour sparingly.

  6. Spread a very thin layer of the meat mixture right to the edges, using the back of a spoon. You should almost be able to see the dough through it.

  7. Slide onto the hot steel and bake for 4 to 6 minutes, until the edges are crisp and the meat is cooked and sizzling.

  8. Pile with parsley and red onion tossed with sumac, squeeze over lemon, roll up tightly and eat with your hands.

Chef’s Tips

  • Thinner is always better, for both dough and topping. A thick lahmacun is just a flatbread.
  • Squeeze the grated vegetables until no more liquid comes out — this is the single most important step.
  • They freeze well half-baked: bake 3 minutes, cool, freeze, then finish for 3 minutes from frozen.

Pairing Suggestions

  • Ayran, the salted yogurt drink, or a cold lager
  • Serve with a shepherd's salad and pickled chillies
  • Finish with baklava

Storage & Reheating

Best straight from the oven. Keeps 2 days; reheat at 220°C / 430°F for 4 minutes.
